title: Escalated items go to a stronger holder, then close with evidence; nothing pages Mark

story.i_want_to: place every escalated item with a stronger holder, first on another machine and then on a larger model, and close it with its evidence when those fail too
story.so_that: no item waits for Mark, no item loops for ever, and nothing posts to draw his attention

rationale: PRD R4: 'An item that reaches the DISPATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS ceiling escalates to a stronger holder: first a holder on another machine, then one on a larger model. When those have failed too, the sweep closes the item with the reason and its evidence.' Today an item at the ceiling escalates over :attempts_exhausted with a reason saying 'A human decides whether to spend another attempt' (retry_ceiling.ex:95-98) and stays there; the only thing that acts on escalated items is EscalationDigestWorker (oban_config.ex:789), which posts a daily channel digest to draw attention. This story refactors that worker into the sweep that acts, using US-52.31's holder edge and US-52.32's verbs, and deletes the digest.

acceptance_criteria.description: Loopctl.Delivery.EscalationSweep.run/2 (now, opts) selects, across tenants and oldest first, at most 100 items whose stage is escalated and whose newest transition into escalated is older than the grace window (default 1800 s); an item held over :review_missing goes to AC-52.34.6, never to the rungs.

For an item with attempts['holder_resolution'] of 0 the sweep re-queues it as actor 'worker:escalation_sweep' over :holder_resolution (Interventions.requeue/4), or re-triages it (Interventions.retriage/4) when no implementer touched it; the event's reason names the rung 'another_machine'.

Placement of an implement or triage dispatch for an item whose attempts['holder_resolution'] is at least 1 excludes every runner named by an earlier runner_dispatches row of that item; when every live runner of the tenant that could take the kind is excluded, placement proceeds without the exclusion and records rung_unattainable: 'another_machine' on the dispatch's ledger row.

For an item with attempts['holder_resolution'] of 1 the sweep re-queues or re-triages it again with rung 'larger_model' when STRONGER_HOLDER_MODEL is set, and placement of an item with attempts['holder_resolution'] of at least 2 sends that value as the dispatch payload's optional model field; when STRONGER_HOLDER_MODEL is unset the rung is skipped and the item is closed (AC-52.34.5).

An item past its last rung is closed by the sweep: escalated -> queued over :holder_resolution, then queued -> failed over the new control-only edge :holders_exhausted in the same transaction, with event data evidence listing every escalation of the item (edge, at, runner name, dispatch id, reason cut to 500 codepoints and flagged untrusted).

An item held over :review_missing past the grace window is never re-queued, re-triaged or closed: the sweep mints a review dispatch for its landed revision (Dispatches.mint_chg_reviewer/4 under the change's chg root, one live per revision) and places it on a runner whose agent is not the implementer's and that ran none of the item's implement dispatches, with rung 'independent_review'; while that dispatch is live the sweep places nothing more for the item.

Loopctl.Workers.EscalationDigestWorker becomes Loopctl.Workers.EscalationSweepWorker (every 5 minutes, unique per period); EscalationInbox.post_digest/2, digest_body/3, digest_key/2 and their constants are deleted, so no code path posts a channel message because an item escalated (except the escalation handoffs release 7 deletes); RetryCeiling.exhausted_reason/2 and the RetryCeiling and StageMachine moduledocs name the count, the ceiling and a different holder instead of saying a human decides.

Two sweep runs, or a sweep and a holder's resolve, on one item transition it once: the sweep's transition is US-52.31's compare-and-set, and a loser answered {:not_escalated, stage} is skipped and counted as :raced, never retried within the run.

test_cases.name: selection: grace window, oldest first, review_missing skipped, all tenants (DataCase)
preconditions: two tenants; escalated items at now-10min, now-40min, now-2h; one item held over :review_missing for 40 min
expected_results: the 2h then 40min items from both tenants, the review_missing item marked for review placement; not the 10min item

test_cases.name: first rung re-queues a worked item and re-triages an untouched one (DataCase)
preconditions: an item escalated over :attempts_exhausted after implementing; an item escalated over :triage_escalate
expected_results: first at queued over holder_resolution, reason rung another_machine; second at detected over retriage

test_cases.name: placement avoids earlier machines, and says so when it cannot (DataCase)
preconditions: runners minis and x1 (fixture(:runner)) both selectable; a queued item with attempts holder_resolution 1 and an earlier runner_dispatches row on minis; a second tenant with one runner
steps: the same in the one-runner tenant
expected_results: only x1; the one runner, with rung_unattainable recorded

test_cases.name: the larger-model rung sends the model, and is skipped when unset (DataCase)
preconditions: an item escalated with attempts holder_resolution 1; stronger_holder_model injected as 'opus' through opts, then nil
steps: EscalationSweep.run(now, stronger_holder_model: 'opus') then DispatchDriver payload for it
on a twin item, run with stronger_holder_model: nil
expected_results: payload model 'opus'; twin closed over holders_exhausted

test_cases.name: the last rung closes with every escalation as evidence (DataCase)
preconditions: an item with attempts holder_resolution 2 and three escalation events with runner names
expected_results: stage failed over holders_exhausted; event data evidence has three entries, reasons capped and untrusted: true

test_cases.name: the ceiling's reason names a different holder (unit)
the crontab runs the sweep and no digest (unit)
sweep racing a holder's resolve transitions once (DataCase, two connections)
preconditions: an escalated item past grace; holder B; Loopctl.Test.ProductionTopology
steps: EscalationSweep.run and Escalations.resolve as B concurrently
expected_results: one holder_resolution event; the sweep reports :raced or B gets not_escalated

test_cases.name: a review_missing hold gets an independent reviewer and is never closed (DataCase)
preconditions: a chg story escalated over :review_missing for 40 min (fixtures from test/loopctl/changes/review_custody_test.exs) with attempts holder_resolution 2; its implement dispatch ran on runner minis under agent A; runners minis (agent A) and x1 (agent C) selectable
expected_results: one review dispatch, a child of the change's chg root, placed on x1; stage still escalated over :review_missing, no holders_exhausted event; the second run mints and places nothing

technical_notes: Rung count: story_stages.attempts counts every non-forward edge by name (StageMachine.counted?/1, stage_machine.ex:857; transition_update/6, stages.ex:2088), so attempts['holder_resolution'] is the number of holder re-queues the item has had; no new column. Holder and sweep re-queues both count, which is the point: each was a different holder's try.

Worker: rename lib/loopctl/workers/escalation_digest_worker.ex (perform/1 at :51 iterates EscalationInbox.all_digest_tenants/1, escalation_inbox.ex:466) into the sweep; rename all_digest_tenants/digest_tenants to escalated_tenants/1 and keep system_agent/2 (escalation_inbox.ex:676), which EscalationHandoffs still calls (escalation_handoffs.ex:162,573). Delete the digest block (escalation_inbox.ex:459-665) and the moduledoc's digest section (:61-73). Crontab line oban_config.ex:789 and the assertion in test/loopctl/oban_plugins_config_test.exs.

Transitions reuse Interventions.requeue/4 and retriage/4 (US-52.32) and Escalations.resolve/3 (US-52.31), called with actor_label 'worker:escalation_sweep', actor_role :agent and an attested [] lineage, the shape EventEffects uses for control writes (stage_machine.ex moduledoc, change-protocol edges).

Close: add {:queued, :failed, :holders_exhausted} to @transitions (stage_machine.ex:286), control-only like @release_escalations (:217), resolution_verdict nil (the issue stays open: no fix shipped and no verdict), and an EscalationInbox reason class is not needed because it never enters escalated.

Exclusion: Loopctl.Agents.Dispatcher.runners/3 (lib/loopctl/agents/dispatcher.ex:329), used by DispatchDriver.available_runners/2 (dispatch_driver.ex:182) and the triage pass, filters out runner ids from runner_dispatches (lib/loopctl/runners/dispatch_record.ex:76-80) for the item; the runner's attested name is runners.name (runner.ex:93).

Model: the dispatch payload's optional model field is an additive runner-contract minor (lib/loopctl/api_spec/runner_contract.ex changelog table); the runner process in runner/ (release 2, README names table: runner source) passes it to claude --model; a runner on an older contract ignores it.

STRONGER_HOLDER_MODEL has no default, like DISPATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS (retry_ceiling.ex:24-31): a larger model is spend. Read it in config/runtime.exs and give it a row in deploy/FLY_SECRETS.md (mix loopctl.check_env_docs). Injected into run/2 as an opt so tests never put_env.
Docs: docs/agent-delivery-loop.md section 8 (:189-200) and the operator settings (:209) say what the sweep does and that nothing needs a human.

Review rung: Dispatches.mint_chg_reviewer/4 (lib/loopctl/dispatches.ex:146) mints the reviewer as ReviewDispatches does for chgd (lib/loopctl/changes/review_dispatches.ex:1-50: one live per (source, change_id, revision), never after a review is recorded), so ReviewCustody.authorize_review/4 (lib/loopctl/changes/review_custody.ex:145-153) accepts its record; the landed revision is the one ensure_landed_review/3 (:272) computes. Runner choice reuses VerifierPlacement's agent-apart rule (lib/loopctl/agents/verifier_placement.ex:90) plus AC-52.34.3's runner exclusion. The reviewer session runs chg review with the minted key; its review_records row lets US-52.31's holder edge release the hold (AC-52.31.5). The runner-side review dispatch kind is an additive runner-contract minor beside the model field.
non_goals: Deleting escalation handoffs and EscalationHandoffWorker: release 7, with the move verb (PRD section 4).
Changing DISPATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS or how a release is counted: RetryCeiling.decide/2 is unchanged.
Recording the review and releasing a :review_missing hold: the reviewer's own review_records write and US-52.31's holder edge; the sweep only places the reviewer.

failure_modes.partition: n/a: the sweep runs inside loopctl against its own Postgres; a runner unreachable at placement is the existing no_runner outcome, retried next pass.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.34.2: the rung is derived from story_stages.attempts and the escalation history from the event log, so a sweep that crashes mid-run resumes from the rows on its next run.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.34.8: each transition is a compare-and-set on escalated, so a second run or a racing holder transitions the item once; the worker is unique per period.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.34.1: at most 100 items per run, oldest first, so a backlog drains over several runs without one run holding connections; each item is its own transaction.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.34.7: the sweep is an Oban cron job on any node; a node that dies mid-run leaves the job to Lifeline and the next run.

definition_of_done: On production, an item escalated over :attempts_exhausted is back at queued within 35 minutes with an event by worker:escalation_sweep, and its next dispatch is on a runner it has not used.
SELECT count(*) FROM story_stages WHERE stage = 'escalated' AND updated_at < now() - interval '3 hours' excluding :review_missing holds returns 0 a day after deploy.
defaults: Grace before the sweep acts: 1800 s, so a holder or Mark may act first (owner may change).
Rungs: another machine, then STRONGER_HOLDER_MODEL, then close; STRONGER_HOLDER_MODEL has no default.
Sweep cadence every 5 minutes, at most 100 items per run.
A sweep close leaves the linked issue open and uncommented: nothing shipped and no verdict was reached.
A :review_missing hold waits for its independent reviewer indefinitely; the sweep never closes it, because closing would drop a landed change's review.
